report_markdown:
## Bottom line
Quillforge is a 2019-founded Austin dashboard maker that cut about 15% of staff in September 2026 while it reorganized around its Business plan [S2][S3]. Budget scrutiny is likely, which makes a spend-analytics pitch relevant. Revenue and funding are not public in anything read.

## Overview and business model
Real-time dashboards for operations teams, sold per user per month [S1][S4].

## Size and funding

| Layoff | about 15% (about 60 people) | 2026-09-17 | reported [S2] |
| Revenue | not found | | |
| Funding | not found | | |

## Products and pricing
Team $49, Business $99 per user per month; Enterprise by quote [S4].

## Customers
Larkspur Foods, Tern Logistics, both named on the company's about page [S1].

## Recent news
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-17 | Layoffs of roughly 15% [S2] |

## Leaders in their own words
Mara Lind, CEO, 2026-09-17: the company "remains focused on profitable growth" [S2].

## Risks
- Medium: the layoffs may slow purchases or change who decides [S2].

## Angle for selling
- Inference: proving return on software spend after a reorganization is the likely pain [S2].
- Inference: show per-team cost visibility against per-user pricing [S4].
- Question: who owns software spend now?
